questions.question: Which of the following statements is true regarding the process by which plants prepare their own food?

options.text: Plants require complex organic compounds from their environment to prepare their food.
The roots of plants are the main sites where photosynthesis occurs.
Plants use sunlight, water, and carbon dioxide to synthesize food, primarily in their leaves through a process called photosynthesis.
Photosynthesis is a process exclusive to animals and some microorganisms to prepare their food.

questions.question: Why is it necessary to periodically add fertilizers or manures to soil used for growing crops?

options.text: To introduce beneficial insects to the soil
To boost the water-holding capacity of the soil only
To replenish nutrients like nitrogen, potassium, and phosphorus
To increase the soil's temperature for optimal plant growth

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **To replenish nutrients like nitrogen, potassium, and phosphorus**

**__Explanation:__**

__
 
• Continuous cropping often depletes the soil of essential nutrients plants need for growth and development, such as nitrogen (N), potassium (K), and phosphorus (P). Nitrogen is crucial for leaf growth and chlorophyll production, phosphorus for root development, energy transfer, and flower and seed production, and potassium for overall plant health and disease resistance.
 
• **Plants** require various nutrients for different physiological functions. Primary nutrients include nitrogen (N), phosphorus (P), and potassium (K), often referred to as NPK.
 
• **Nitrogen** is pivotal for vegetative growth, being a key component of chlorophyll and amino acids.
 
• **Phosphorus** is essential for energy transfer within plants, rooting, and blooming, while **potassium** plays a critical role in cell function, water uptake, and resistance to stresses.
 
• Fertilizers and manures are added to the soil to replenish these nutrients, ensuring that crops receive the necessary elements to grow effectively. While manures are organic and release nutrients slowly, fertilizers can be organic or inorganic, often providing a quicker supply of specific nutrients.
 
• The application of these substances helps maintain soil fertility, support high crop yields, and improve the overall health of crops.

**Conclusion:__**

The periodic addition of fertilizers and manures is vital to replenish soil nutrients that are continually depleted by crop production. This practice supports soil fertility, enhances plant growth and yield, and is a cornerstone of successful and sustainable agricultural systems

questions.question: Association of two different organisms in which both are benefited is called-
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Symbiosis.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• Organisms that live together and share shelter and nutrients is called a **symbiotic relationship.**
 
• In a symbiotic relationship, **both organisms are benefited.**
 
• Some** fungi that live in the roots of trees** are an example of a symbiotic relationship.
 
 
• The tree provides nutrients to the fungus and, in return, receives help from it to take up water and nutrients from the soil.
 
 
 
• **Lichens** are an example of a symbiotic relationship between algae and certain fungi.
 
 
• The fungus provides shelter, water, and minerals to the algae and, in return, the algae provides food which it prepares by photosynthesis.
 
 
 
• **Tapeworms that **live in the small intestines of animals are an example of a symbiotic relationship.
 
• The relationship between an **anemone and a clownfish** is a classic example of symbiosis.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Nutrition** is the process by which the organism ingests, digests, absorbs, transports, and utilizes nutrients and disposes of its end-products.
 
• The organisms that derive their food from dead and rotten material are called **saprophytes.**
 
• The organisms that live on or inside other living organisms to derive their food are called **parasites.**

questions.question: The mode of nutrition in which organisms take in nutrients from dead and decaying matter is called ______ nutrition.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Saprotropic.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Saprotrophic nutrition** is the mode of nutrition in which **organisms obtain nutrients by decomposing dead and decaying organic matter.**
 
• Saprotrophs, also known as **decomposers**, secrete digestive enzymes to break down complex organic compounds into simpler substances.
 
• They absorb the nutrients from the decomposed matter, playing** a vital role in recycling nutrients back into the ecosystem.**
 
• **Examples** of saprotrophs include** fungi **(such as mushrooms and moulds) and **certain bacteria.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Autotrophic:**

 
 
• Autotrophic nutrition is the mode of nutrition in which organisms can** synthesize their own food using inorganic substances and an external energy source.**
 
• Autotrophs** convert sunlight or inorganic compounds into organic compounds** through photosynthesis or chemosynthesis.
 
• They include **green plants, algae, and some bacteria.**
 
• Autotrophs are **primary producers in food chains**, serving as a source of energy for heterotrophs.
 
 
 
• **Heterotrophic:**
 
 
• Heterotrophic nutrition is the mode of nutrition in which **organisms obtain their food by consuming organic matter produced by other organisms.**
 
• Heterotrophs cannot **synthesize their own food and rely on consuming plants, animals, or other organic materials for nutrients.**
 
• Examples of heterotrophs include** animals, fungi** (except for a few species), and **most bacteria.**
 
• Heterotrophs play important roles **as consumers and decomposers** in food chains and nutrient cycles.
 
 
 
• **Monostrophic:**
 
 
• A monographic diet, also known as the** mono diet or single-food diet,** involves** eating only one food item or one type of food.**
 
• Examples of monotrophic diets include** consuming solely potatoes or apples or restricting oneself to fruits or meats.**
 
• Monotrophic diets may be followed for reasons such as **food faddism, crash dieting, initiating an elimination diet, or exploring extreme forms of alternative medicine.**

questions.question: Which of the following is the ultimate source of energy for all living organisms?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Sun.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The ultimate source of energy for all living organisms is the** sun.**
 
• The sun provides energy to plants through the process of **photosynthesis. **
 
• Animals then **consume plant**s (or other animals that have consumed plants) to obtain energy. 
 
• This energy is then used for various processes such as** growth, reproduction, and movement. **
 
• Without the sun,** life on Earth** would not be possible.​

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Soil:** While soil does provide nutrients and water to plants, it is **not** the ultimate source of energy for living organisms.
 
• **Water:** Water is essential for life, but it is** not** a direct source of energy.
 
• **Air:** While oxygen is required for respiration, it is **not** the ultimate source of energy.

questions.question: How does the bacterium Rhizobium benefit leguminous plants?

options.text: By decomposing organic matter in the soil
By converting atmospheric nitrogen into a usable form for the plants
By acting as a natural pesticide against soil-borne pathogens
By aerating the soil around the plant roots

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **By converting atmospheric nitrogen into a usable form for the plants**

**__Explanation:__**

__
 
• **Rhizobium **is a genus of bacteria known for its ability to form symbiotic associations with leguminous plants, such as peas, beans, and other members of the legume family. These bacteria inhabit root nodules of the plants and fix atmospheric nitrogen (N₂), converting it into ammonium (NH₄⁺), a form of nitrogen that plants can readily use for their growth and development. This process is known as biological nitrogen fixation.
 
• The relationship is mutually beneficial: the plant provides the Rhizobium with carbohydrates and a protective environment within the root nodules, while the bacteria supply the plant with fixed nitrogen, significantly contributing to its nitrogen needs.
 
• This symbiotic relationship allows leguminous plants to thrive in nitrogen-poor soils where other plants may struggle.

(a) While decomposing organic matter in the soil is essential for nutrient recycling, it is not the primary role of Rhizobium in its relationship with leguminous plants.

(c) Rhizobium might indirectly influence soil health, their primary benefit to legumes is not acting as a natural pesticide against soil-borne pathogens.

(d) Aerating the soil around the plant roots is not the role of Rhizobium. Their main function is nitrogen fixation within the root nodules of legumes.

**Conclusion:__**

Thus, Option (b) accurately describes how Rhizobium benefits leguminous plants.

questions.question: What is the symbiotic relationship between certain fungi and the roots of plants called?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is** ****Mutualism**

**__Explanation:__**

__
 
• **Mutualism** is a type of symbiotic relationship where both parties involved benefit from the association.
 
• In the context of the relationship between certain fungi and plant roots, this mutualism is specifically known as mycorrhiza.
 
• In this relationship, the fungi colonize the plant roots, extending their network beyond the root system, which greatly increases the plant's access to water and nutrients such as phosphorus and nitrogen from the soil. In return, the plant supplies the fungi with carbohydrates derived from photosynthesis.
 
• This mutualistic relationship enhances plant growth, stress resistance, and nutrient absorption, while providing the fungi with the energy resources they need to thrive.

(a) **Parasitism** describes a relationship where one organism benefits at the expense of another.

(c) **Predation** is an interaction where one organism preys upon another.

(d) **Commensalism **is a relationship where one organism benefits and the other is neither helped nor harmed.

**Conclusion:__**

Therefore, (b) Mutualism is the correct answer.

questions.question: Identify the set that correctly groups all autotrophic organisms:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Grass, Algae, Trees**

**__Explanation:__**

**Autotrophic organisms** are those that can produce their own food, typically through photosynthesis, using light energy from the sun, carbon dioxide, and water to produce glucose and oxygen. This process is fundamental to the energy flow through ecosystems, as autotrophs are primary producers on which other, non-photosynthetic organisms depend.

__
 
• **Grass, Algae, Trees:** All of these are capable of photosynthesis. Grass and trees are terrestrial plants, and algae are typically aquatic organisms. All possess chlorophyll for capturing sunlight and converting it into chemical energy.
 
• **Algae**: Present in both the correct group and option (d), algae are indeed autotrophic, harnessing sunlight to produce organic compounds from carbon dioxide and water.
 
• **Cuscuta** is a parasitic plant, which does not perform photosynthesis to a significant extent and instead derives nutrients by attaching to other, photosynthetically active (autotrophic) plants. Therefore, option (a) is not entirely composed of autotrophs.
 
• **Moss, Ferns **are both photosynthetic and thus autotrophic. However, the **Pitcher plant **is a carnivorous plant that still relies on photosynthesis but also supplements its nutrient intake by capturing insects. This mix doesn't represent a group of exclusively autotrophic organisms in the strictest sense even though all can carry out photosynthesis.
 
• **Fungi **are heterotrophic organisms, not autotrophic. They obtain their food by absorbing nutrients from their external environment, often breaking down dead organic matter.

**Conclusion:__**

 Therefore, the correct group of autotrophic organisms includes **Grass, Algae, Trees**

questions.question:
Match the following terms with their correct descriptions:

 
 

 
 **Column A**
 
 **Column B**
 
 

 i
 Cuscuta
 a
 Parasite
 
 

 ii
 Pitcher Plant
 b
 Symbiotic Relationship
 
 

 iii
 Rhizobium
 c
 Insectivorous Plant
questions.solution:
The correct answer is** ****(i) - (a), (ii) - (c), (iii) - (b)**

**__Explanation:__**

**(i) Cuscuta - (a) Parasite**

 
• Cuscuta is commonly known as dodder and is a genus of over 200 species of yellow, orange, or red (rarely green) parasitic plants. Unlike most plants, dodder lacks chlorophyll, which is necessary for photosynthesis, and cannot produce its food.
 
• Therefore, it relies entirely on a host plant to provide the water and nutrients it needs.
 
• Cuscuta has a specialized structure known as haustoria, which penetrates the host plant's vascular tissue to draw water and nutrients directly from it.
 
• This dependency on another living organism for nutrients classifies Cuscuta as a parasitic plant.

**(ii) Pitcher Plant - (c) Insectivorous Plant**

 
• The Pitcher Plant refers to several different carnivorous plants with specialized leaves known as pitfall traps-a prey-trapping mechanism featuring a deep cavity filled with digestive fluid.
 
• The plants lure insects and small animals with nectar and coloration into their "pitcher," from which the prey cannot escape.
 
• Once the organism falls in, it drowns and is digested by the plant, providing it with much-needed nitrogen and other nutrients that are often scarce in the environments where these plants typically grow, such as nutrient-poor, acidic bogs.

**(iii) Rhizobium - (b) Symbiotic Relationship**

 
• Rhizobium is a genus of bacteria that forms a symbiotic relationship with legumes (plants in the family Fabaceae). These bacteria colonize the plant roots and form specialized structures called nodules.
 
• Inside these nodules, Rhizobium bacteria convert atmospheric nitrogen, which plants cannot use directly, into a form of nitrogen (ammonia) that plants can use for growth. This process is known as nitrogen fixation.
 
• In exchange, the plant supplies the bacteria with carbohydrates produced through photosynthesis. This mutualistic relationship is beneficial for both organisms and plays a crucial role in the nitrogen cycle, contributing to the fertility of the soil.
